planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; Amber Gem is part of the Winter Jewels breeding series, with warm amber-gold flowers blooming in late winter to early spring.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, keeping soil evenly moist while the plant establishes. Amber Gem is part of the acclaimed Winter Jewels hellebore breeding series, producing rounded, outward-facing flowers in warm amber, apricot, and honey tones often accented with darker veining or a subtle picotee edge, held above leathery, evergreen, deeply divided foliage. Like other Lenten roses it blooms very early, often pushing through late-season snow or hard frost, providing reliable color in the shade garden when little else is flowering. Remove tattered old foliage in late winter just before bloom to showcase the flowers at their best, and site it away from areas where pets or children graze, since all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
sources: Northwest Garden Nursery — Winter Jewels hellebore breeding
